title: Zen and Creativity Class 2 Part 2
speaker: Shuko Edie Norton
summary: Shuko Edie Norton looks at how haiku are put together, reading through a list of poems by Basho and Issa, including the wind from Mount Fuji painted on a fan, a sleeping rider with the far moon in a continuing dream, and a line about steam from roasting tea. Shuko points out that the third line can seem unrelated or arrive as an unexpected sound, and that a poem can run two, three, or four lines. The group wonders whether the originals keep the 5-7-5 syllable count and why Issa's translations read lighter and more efficient than Basho's. Shuko then suggests choosing an ordinary object such as a chair or pillow and looking at it closely, and describes trying to see where a shadow would fall when painting.
